result.title: DynaCue: Comparing Motion and Timing Between Groups of Videos
result.summary: A score that distinguishes videos with different temporal-consistency ratings can miss differences associated with motion preference. VideoScore's temporal consistency score distinguished higher- from lower-rated Pika videos in 95% of comparisons with 15 videos per group, yet could not detect the difference between preferred videos and their same-prompt alternatives in any of the 200 comparisons of 41 VideoGen-RewardBench pairs. We introduce DynaCue, a two-sample permutation test that combines complementary measurements of motion, frame continuity, and appearance to compare groups of videos without choosing a single cue in advance. DynaCue measures local changes in optical flow both before and after accounting for each clip's usual activity, captures interruptions through frame differences and freeze counts, and incorporates scores for motion and appearance. In controlled experiments, DynaCue detected group differences across five interventions affecting playback continuity, displacement, or rhythm. In real-world evaluations of generated videos where viewers rated temporal consistency or chose which of two videos they preferred for its motion, DynaCue detected group differences in at least 80% of resampled comparisons on each of the three datasets at the smaller sample sizes studied. Every other method evaluated on all three had a detection rate of 60% or less on at least one dataset.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 DynaCue，用两样本置换检验结合光流局部变化、帧差与冻结计数以及运动/外观评分，来比较两组视频在时序一致性与运动偏好上的差异，并在受控干预与真实生成视频评分数据上验证其检测率。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作属于视频生成的质量/运动评价指标，衡量的是输出像素层面的时序连贯性，未涉及模型内部状态、视觉证据筛选、推理与停止决策；其置换检验仅是通用统计手段，缺乏可供核查的 LVR 迁移线索，故排除。
